scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus in a cream robe and brown shawl walks up a rocky path toward Jerusalem's sunlit walls. Other travelers and a donkey approach the city, where crowds gather beneath colorful cloths near the gate.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative portrayal of Jesus going up to Jerusalem when a Jewish feast was taking place, as described in John 5:1. The feast is unnamed; the travelers, decorations, cityscape, and figures' appearances are artistic additions.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A sunlit stone pool divided by a covered central walkway and surrounded by four roofed, columned porticoes, with sheep beside a gate in Jerusalem's city wall.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative view of the pool by Jerusalem's Sheep Gate, which John 5:2 describes as having five porticoes. The layout, architecture, and sheep are artistic choices, not details specified by the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: People rest on woven mats beneath stone colonnades beside a pool; a man leans on crutches, an older man holds a walking staff, and a woman lies near the water.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts the multitude of ailing people lying near the pool in John 5:3 and awaiting the movement of the water. The awaiting phrase falls within a passage marked with parentheses in the pinned Nestle 1904 text.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An angel with glowing wings stirs a stone pool as a man steps into the water, while other people wait beside the pool beneath a colonnade.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene pictures the angel stirring the pool and the first person entering after the stirring, whom John 5:4 describes as made well. Nestle 1904 prints John 5:3-4 in parentheses; the English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A man reclines on a woven mat beside a sunlit pool beneath stone colonnades, while others rest in the shade behind him.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: John 5:5 describes a man who had been ill for thirty-eight years. This imaginative scene places him beside the pool and colonnades described in the surrounding passage.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus kneels beside a man lying on a mat and speaks to him near a pool surrounded by stone colonnades.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of John 5:6, when Jesus sees a man who has been ill a long time lying down and asks whether he wants to become well. The pool and colonnade draw on the surrounding passage.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Beside a stone pool, an ailing man on a mat gestures toward a person entering the water while Jesus listens; others sit beneath a sunlit colonnade.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene brings the man's account of having no one to put him into the stirred water, and of another going down before him, into his conversation with Jesus in John 5:7. It does not claim that these actions occurred at the same moment.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward a man rising beside a stone pool and reaching for a woven mat; other people rest beneath the colonnade behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene portrays Jesus instructing the man in John 5:8 to arise, take up his mat, and walk. The setting, poses, and appearances are artistic interpretations.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A man walks beside a stone-lined pool, carrying a rolled woven mat under his arm while people gather beneath sunlit colonnades.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined scene depicts John 5:9, when the man immediately became well, took up his mat and began to walk on the Sabbath. The pool and porticoes come from the surrounding account in John 5:2; their appearance and the figures are artistic interpretation.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone street, a man holds a rolled woven mat while three men face him and two gesture toward him.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts John 5:10, where Jewish people tell the man who had been healed that it is the Sabbath and he may not take up his mat. The setting, appearance, and gestures are imagined.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A man carrying a rolled mat gestures as he speaks with two listeners on a sunlit stone walkway beside a pool.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of the healed man answering that the one who made him well told him to take up his mat and walk, as in John 5:11. The setting and appearances are artistic interpretations.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two men question a man holding a rolled sleeping mat on a sunlit stone street; one gestures with open hands as the man looks uncertain.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of the question in John 5:12. The rolled mat draws on John 5:11. The verse's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A man holding a rolled mat stands beside a pool under sunlit stone columns, looking toward a crowd in which a robed figure walks away.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative portrayal of John 5:13: the man who had been healed did not know who Jesus was, and Jesus had moved away while a crowd was there. The setting and poses are interpretive; the verse relationship follows the chapter's Berean Interlinear token glosses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit temple court, Jesus rests a hand on a man's shoulder and gestures as the man listens, holding a rolled woven mat.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts John 5:14, where Jesus finds the man made well in the temple and warns him to sin no more so that nothing worse may happen. The mat recalls the earlier account; its presence at this meeting is imagined.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A smiling man holding a rolled mat speaks to two listeners and gestures toward Jesus walking down a sunlit stone street.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of the man telling the Jews that Jesus had made him well. The street, gestures, listeners, and Jesus appearing in the distance are artistic choices rather than details specified in John 5:15.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands beside a stone colonnade facing several men who gesture toward him, while another man carries a rolled mat beside the pool.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined confrontation illustrates John 5:16's account of Jews persecuting Jesus because he was doing these things on the Sabbath. The man carrying a mat recalls the healing in the preceding passage.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits among attentive listeners and gestures as he speaks in a sunlit stone colonnade. Behind them, a man carries a rolled mat beside a pool.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene of Jesus answering his listeners, reflecting John 5:17's statement that his Father is working until now and that he too is working. The man carrying a mat recalls the healing earlier in John 5; the setting, gestures and arrangement are imagined. The verse's token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear, not a GBT approval.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures upward in a sunlit stone courtyard while several men confer tensely nearby; a man behind him carries a rolled mat.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene relates to John 5:18, where the Jews seek all the more to kill Jesus because he was breaking the Sabbath and called God his own Father, making himself equal with God. The man carrying a mat recalls the healing in the surrounding passage; the setting and gestures are imagined. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, not GBT-approved glosses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits in a sunlit stone courtyard, speaking to listeners and raising one hand toward the sky, while a smiling man stands nearby carrying a rolled mat.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene represents Jesus explaining that the Son does what he sees the Father doing. The man with the mat recalls the earlier healing in John 5; the verse does not describe these visual details.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus looks and gestures toward sunlight beside a man holding a rolled mat, while onlookers watch in wonder by a pool with stone colonnades.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined scene reflects John 5:20: the light suggests the Father's love for the Son and the works He shows Him, while the onlookers and distant brightness evoke the greater works to come and the wonder they will inspire. The man with the mat and the pool recall the earlier healing in John 5; this particular scene is not described as an event in verse 20. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear, not GBT-approved glosses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus reaches for the hand of a man rising from a stone tomb, wrapped in burial cloth, amid flowers on a sunlit hillside.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative visual meditation on John 5:21: the Father raises the dead and gives life, and the Son gives life to whom he wills. The image does not depict a specific event narrated in this verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits on a stone seat holding bronze balance scales in a beam of golden light as people watch nearby, with olive trees and a hillside village in the background.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative portrayal of John 5:22: the scales and heavenly light suggest the Father's gift of all judgment to the Son. The scene is an artistic illustration, not an event described in the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures to an attentive group in a sunlit stone courtyard while one man turns away at the edge.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined scene reflects John 5:23's teaching that honoring the Son is inseparable from honoring the Father who sent him; the sunlight is symbolic, not a literal depiction of the Father.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks to a listener stepping from barren, stony ground toward a sunlit path lined with flowers.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene suggests John 5:24 through a change from barren ground to a flowering path. The verse says that the one who hears Jesus' word and believes the One who sent Him has eternal life, does not come into judgment, and has passed out of death into life. Its English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus reaches toward people rising among rocks and wildflowers near a stone tomb, with a sunlit landscape behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative illustration of Jesus' words that the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live. The awakening figures are a visual metaphor, not an event narrated in this verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus stands in a flower-filled garden on a Judean hillside, one hand over his glowing chest and the other extended toward a green sapling beneath a sunlit sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene uses the Son's inner light and the light of the sky as a visual metaphor for John 5:26: as the Father has life in Himself, He has given the Son to have life in Himself.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits on a raised stone seat holding balanced scales as people gather around him in a sunlit courtyard, with olive trees and hills beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene uses scales and light from the sky to suggest the authority the Father gives the Son of Man to execute judgment in John 5:27. The setting, people and visual symbols are artistic inventions.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward men and women listening from open stone tombs in a sunlit hillside.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene depicts the coming hour in John 5:28, when all those in the tombs will hear his voice. The setting, appearances, and gestures are artistic choices. The verse's English word glosses come from the Berean Interlinear and are not a Global Bible Tools approval.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: People emerge from rock-hewn tombs; some walk toward a sunlit garden, while others climb steps toward a seated figure in a stone court.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects John 5:29, contrasting the resurrection of life for those who have done good with the resurrection of judgment for those who have done evil. The tombs recall the preceding verse; the garden, court, appearances, and setting are artistic choices. The chapter's English word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear and are not a Global Bible Tools approval.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits in a sunlit stone courtyard, looking upward and extending an open hand toward several people. A balanced bronze scale stands on a low table beside Him.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene evokes John 5:30: Jesus judges as He hears, and His judgment is just because He seeks the will of the One who sent Him rather than His own. The courtyard, people, and balance are artistic choices, not details stated in the verse. The English token glosses are from the Berean Interlinear Bible, not GBT-approved glosses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward his chest while speaking to listeners in a sunlit stone courtyard; his face is reflected in a basin of water.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative teaching scene uses the gesture and reflection to evoke John 5:31's conditional statement about Jesus bearing witness concerning Himself and His testimony not being true. The courtyard and reflection are artistic details, not details specified in the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits and gestures as a group of listeners gathers around him in a sunlit stone courtyard, with an archway and greenery behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene pictures Jesus speaking about the true testimony another bears concerning him. The sunlight is a visual suggestion, not a depiction or identification of the witness.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: John the Baptist, wearing rough brown clothing, gestures toward three listening men on a sunlit riverbank.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: John 5:33 says people were sent to John and that he bore witness to the truth. This imaginative scene shows him speaking with them beside the Jordan.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits in a sunlit stone courtyard and gestures with an open hand while several people listen; a path leads toward a city gate behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene evokes John 5:34: Jesus says he does not receive testimony from a person, but speaks these things so that his listeners may be saved. The setting and poses are imagined. The relationship follows the pinned Greek text and Berean Interlinear token glosses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: John the Baptist, wearing a rough brown garment, speaks to a smiling gathering around a burning oil lamp set on a stone at dusk.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative depiction of Jesus' description of John as a burning, shining lamp and of people rejoicing for a time in his light. The gathering and physical lamp visualize the metaphor rather than document an event.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks with open hands beside a pool as a smiling man carries a rolled mat and onlookers watch.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined moment connects Jesus' statement that the works the Father gave him testify that the Father sent him with the healing and carried mat earlier in John 5.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus sits on stone steps in a sunlit courtyard, gesturing as five men listen; leafy vines and distant hillside buildings frame the gathering.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene shows Jesus addressing listeners as he speaks of the Father who sent him and bore witness about him. John 5:37 says they have neither heard the Father's voice nor seen his form. The chapter's word glosses are from the Berean Interlinear, not a GBT approval.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks with open hands to a group in a sunlit stone courtyard; one listener turns away while holding a rolled scroll.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene evokes John 5:38: God’s word does not abide in the listeners, who do not believe the one He sent. The relationship follows the verse’s Berean Interlinear token glosses; the scene is not presented as a recorded historical event.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward an unrolled scroll as four listeners gather around it in a sunlit stone courtyard with vines and greenery.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects John 5:39: Jesus speaks of people searching the Scriptures because they think they have eternal life in them, and says that the Scriptures bear witness concerning him. The English token glosses used for this interpretation are from the Berean Interlinear Bible and are marked uncurated in the lesson data, not GBT-approved.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus extends an open hand toward four listeners who stand apart with their gazes lowered or turned away, in a sunlit stone courtyard beside flowers, greenery, and flowing water.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined scene illustrates John 5:40: Jesus speaks of people who are unwilling to come to him to have life. The courtyard, garden, and water are artistic choices, with the living plants and water suggesting life.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus raises an open hand toward a man offering a laurel wreath while other men watch in a sunlit stone courtyard.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene uses the offered wreath as a symbol of human glory, which Jesus says he does not receive in John 5:41. The wreath and courtyard are illustrative details, not events stated in the verse. The token glosses used are from the Berean Interlinear.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, Jesus gestures toward a group of men, some sitting with folded arms or looking away.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: An imaginative scene for John 5:42, in which Jesus says that he knows his hearers and that they do not have the love of God in themselves. The courtyard, gestures, and expressions are artistic interpretation. The verse's English word glosses are from the uncurated Berean Interlinear Bible.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, Jesus speaks with open hands while some listeners turn away; nearby, a richly dressed man gestures toward himself as smiling people welcome him.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects John 5:43: Jesus says he has come in his Father's name and is not received, while another coming in his own name would be received. The second figure illustrates the verse's conditional contrast and is not an identification of a historical person. The verse relationship follows the Berean Interlinear token glosses in the source file, not a GBT approval.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, Jesus gestures toward the sky while one man places a leafy wreath on another and others watch.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene for John 5:44 uses a wreath to suggest receiving glory from one another and a gesture toward the light to suggest the glory from the only God that the listeners do not seek. The verse asks how they can believe; it does not describe the pictured event.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks with an open hand to listeners in a sunlit stone courtyard. An imagined Moses stands behind them holding two blank tablets, while one listener holds a scroll.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative scene reflects John 5:45: Jesus tells his listeners not to suppose that he will accuse them before the Father, because Moses, in whom they have hoped, is their accuser. Moses is shown as a visual evocation, not as a claim that he was physically present.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus gestures toward a blank scroll held by a listener as others gather around him in a sunlit stone courtyard.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined scene illustrates John 5:46, where Jesus connects believing Moses with believing him because Moses wrote about him. The courtyard, listeners, and scroll are artistic choices, not details specified in the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Jesus speaks with open hands to a group of listeners beside an unmarked scroll on a low table in a sunny stone courtyard.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: In this imaginative scene, the blank scroll represents Moses' writings as Jesus asks how his listeners will believe his words if they do not believe those writings. The chapter's English word glosses come from the Berean Interlinear.
